questions.q: Why does dynamic RLS scale better than static, per-value roles?
options: A single dynamic role filters differently for each signed-in user via a user-mapping table, instead of needing one static role per value
Dynamic RLS doesn't actually filter any data, it just labels it
Static roles automatically convert to dynamic roles after 30 days
Dynamic RLS requires fewer DAX functions than static RLS
questions.explain: Instead of one role per region/territory/value, dynamic RLS uses one role whose filter expression adapts per user, matched against a user-mapping table.

questions.q: What is the most common cause of dynamic RLS 'not working' in practice?
options: The user-mapping table's values don't match the exact format USERPRINCIPALNAME() or USERNAME() returns in the service
Dynamic RLS is fundamentally incompatible with Import mode
The DAX filter expression syntax is always wrong
Dynamic RLS requires a Premium capacity to function at all
questions.explain: A format mismatch between the mapping table's stored values and what the function actually returns in the service is the classic dynamic-RLS bug — always verify the returned format, don't assume it.

questions.q: What identity does the Test as role feature use when evaluating a dynamic RLS filter?
options: Your own identity — USERPRINCIPALNAME() returns your UPN, not the UPN of whoever you're trying to simulate
The identity of a randomly chosen workspace member
No identity at all — it evaluates the filter as always TRUE
The identity of the semantic model's original owner, permanently
questions.explain: Test as role simulates role membership, but the dynamic function evaluation still uses your own signed-in identity — it can't reveal what a specific other person's UPN would resolve to.

questions.q: How does USERNAME() behave differently in Power BI Desktop versus the Power BI service?
options: In Desktop it returns DOMAIN\username; in the service it returns the User Principal Name (UPN) format
It behaves identically in both places, always returning an email address
It only works in the service, never in Desktop
It returns a numeric user ID in both places
questions.explain: This format difference between Desktop and the service is exactly why testing in Desktop alone can be misleading — always verify the actual format returned once published.

questions.q: What is a user-mapping table in the context of dynamic RLS?
options: A small table pairing each user's UPN/email with the data (e.g. territory) they should be allowed to see
A table that lists every Power BI license type available
A table required only for static RLS, never dynamic
An automatically generated table Power BI creates with no user input
questions.explain: The user-mapping table is the piece that makes dynamic RLS work — it's a manually built table relating each user's identity to whatever value should filter their view.
